Clinical ROC Analysis

Source: R/enhancedROC.h.R
enhancedROC.Rd

Clinical ROC analysis toolkit for comprehensive diagnostic performance evaluation. Includes ROC curve analysis, Youden Index optimization, sensitivity/specificity analysis, optimal cutoff determination, and comparative ROC analysis. Essential for biomarker validation, diagnostic test evaluation, and clinical decision support in medical research.

Usage

enhancedROC(
  data,
  outcome,
  positiveClass,
  predictors,
  analysisType = "single",
  direction = "higher",
  youdenOptimization = TRUE,
  customCutoffs = "",
  sensitivityThreshold = 0,
  specificityThreshold = 0,
  confidenceLevel = 95,
  bootstrapSamples = 1000,
  useBootstrap = FALSE,
  bootstrapMethod = "bca",
  bootstrapPartialAUC = FALSE,
  stratifiedBootstrap = FALSE,
  seed = 0,
  pairwiseComparisons = FALSE,
  comparisonMethod = "delong",
  rocCurve = TRUE,
  aucTable = TRUE,
  cutoffTable = FALSE,
  optimalCutoffs = TRUE,
  diagnosticMetrics = TRUE,
  clinicalMetrics = FALSE,
  smoothMethod = "none",
  partialAuc = FALSE,
  partialAucType = "specificity",
  partialAucFrom = 0.8,
  partialAucTo = 1,
  crocAnalysis = FALSE,
  crocAlpha = 7,
  convexHull = FALSE,
  detectImbalance = FALSE,
  imbalanceThreshold = 3,
  showImbalanceWarning = FALSE,
  recommendPRC = FALSE,
  prevalence = 0.1,
  useObservedPrevalence = TRUE,
  clinicalContext = "general",
  clinicalPresets = "custom",
  comprehensive_output = FALSE,
  clinical_interpretation = FALSE,
  showAnalysisSummary = FALSE,
  showClinicalReport = FALSE,
  showTableNotes = FALSE,
  plotTheme = "jamovi",
  plotWidth = 600,
  plotHeight = 600,
  showCutoffPoints = FALSE,
  showConfidenceBands = FALSE,
  showMetricsDiff = FALSE,
  statisticalComparison = FALSE,
  calibrationAnalysis = FALSE,
  calibrationPlot = FALSE,
  hosmerLemeshow = FALSE,
  hlGroups = 10,
  brierScore = FALSE,
  calibrationMetrics = FALSE,
  splineCalibration = FALSE,
  splineKnots = 4,
  eoRatio = FALSE,
  calibrationDensity = FALSE,
  multiClassROC = FALSE,
  multiClassStrategy = "ovr",
  multiClassAveraging = "macro",
  clinicalImpact = FALSE,
  nntCalculation = FALSE,
  clinicalUtilityCurve = FALSE,
  decisionImpactTable = FALSE,
  internalValidation = FALSE,
  validationMethod = "bootstrap",
  decisionImpactCurves = FALSE,
  impactCutoffs = "0.5",
  utilityThreshold = 0.1,
  workloadPopulationSize = 1000,
  analysisUnit = "slide",
  prevalenceScenarios = "",
  validationPanel = FALSE,
  validationNegative,
  referenceDescription = "",
  modelVersion = "",
  cohortRole = "frozen",
  samplingDesign = "other",
  thresholdSource = "prespecified",
  predictionScale = "score",
  patientID = NULL,
  siteID = NULL,
  partitionID = NULL,
  validationBootstrap = FALSE,
  validationDraws = 999
)

Arguments

data

The data as a data frame.

outcome

Outcome variable (disease status). A factor with two levels, or with more than two (choose one as Positive class and the others are pooled as negative, or use Multi-class ROC). A numeric outcome must have exactly two values; 0/1 reads 1 as positive. Each row must be a different patient: every interval and test assumes independent rows.

positiveClass

Level of outcome treated as the positive class (condition present), matched exactly. Pass NULL to leave it unset: a numeric outcome coded 0/1 then reads 1 as positive, and any other outcome leaves the analysis waiting for a choice, because levels are never chosen from their order. Every other level is analyzed as negative (pooled when there are more than two). A numeric outcome must have exactly two values; to choose among more, make it a factor.

predictors

Numeric predictor variables for ROC analysis, one value per patient (row).

analysisType

Single analyses each predictor on its own; Comparative adds the pairwise comparison tables and the comparative ROC plot. Comprehensive Diagnostic Performance currently gives the same output as Single.

direction

Direction of the predictor-outcome relationship. The default is "Higher values indicate positive outcome" because it is a stated hypothesis rather than an estimate. "Auto" reads the orientation off the same data that supply the AUC - pROC compares the two groups' median values

  • so the direction is fitted rather than assumed, and every AUC is biased upward (for n = 20 the AUC expected under no association is about 0.60, not 0.50, and exceeds 0.60 in roughly 45 of every 100 markers carrying no information at all). It is not floored at 0.5 either: a median split can disagree with the ranks, so about 12 of those 100 null markers are still reported below 0.5. "Auto" can also silently invert a marker and report 0.825 where the un-inverted reading is 0.175. Use "Auto" only for exploratory screening of markers whose direction is genuinely unknown, and say so.

youdenOptimization

Find the optimal cutoff by maximizing the Youden index (sensitivity + specificity - 1), subject to the minimum sensitivity/specificity below. When off, the cutoff closest to the top-left corner of the ROC curve is reported instead. The minimum sensitivity and specificity are used only by the Youden search; with this off they are not applied and a warning says so.

customCutoffs

Comma-separated list of custom cutoffs to evaluate (e.g., 0.1, 0.5, 0.9)

sensitivityThreshold

Minimum sensitivity a cutoff must achieve to be considered. 0 (the default) searches for the overall Youden optimum with no constraint. Raising it restricts the search, which is what you want for a screening test, but the reported cutoff is then the best one meeting your minimum rather than the Youden maximum - a notice says so when the two differ. Used only when Youden index optimization is on.

specificityThreshold

Minimum specificity a cutoff must achieve to be considered. 0 (the default) searches for the overall Youden optimum with no constraint. Raising it restricts the search, which is what you want for a confirmatory test, but the reported cutoff is then the best one meeting your minimum rather than the Youden maximum - a notice says so when the two differ. Used only when Youden index optimization is on.

confidenceLevel

Confidence level for AUC confidence intervals

bootstrapSamples

Number of resamples for every resampling step except the frozen-model report: bootstrap confidence intervals (AUC, partial AUC, multi-class), the ROC confidence bands, the bootstrap comparison test, and the number of permutations for Venkatraman's test. With B permutations no p-value below 1/(B + 1) can be shown, so keep at least 1000 for a test.

useBootstrap

Use bootstrap methods for confidence intervals

bootstrapMethod

Method for calculating bootstrap confidence intervals. BCa corrects for bias and skewness and is second-order accurate in large samples; for a single AUC in small samples no interval method is uniformly best (Obuchowski and Lieber 1998; Feng et al. 2017).

bootstrapPartialAUC

Bootstrap confidence interval for the partial AUC, using the resample count, interval type (BCa/percentile/basic) and stratification set above. The interval is for the raw partial AUC on the chosen focus range, not for the McClish-normalized value.

stratifiedBootstrap

Resample cases and controls separately, keeping the outcome proportions, in every bootstrap of this analysis: the AUC and partial-AUC intervals, the bootstrap comparison test and the ROC confidence bands (recommended for imbalanced data). Off by default: unticked, these bootstraps resample patients without regard to outcome.

seed

Random seed used for every resampling step - bootstrap confidence intervals, bootstrap ROC comparisons, and internal validation resamples or cross-validation folds. Each step starts from this seed, so a predictor's result does not depend on which predictors or options were resampled before it. Fixing it makes a run reproducible: the same data and options give the same intervals every time. Change it to check how sensitive a result is to the particular resamples drawn.

pairwiseComparisons

Perform pairwise comparisons between ROC curves

comparisonMethod

Method for comparing ROC curves. DeLong et al. (1988) and Bootstrap test whether the two AUCs differ. The Venkatraman permutation test (Venkatraman & Begg 1996, paired data) tests whether the two ROC curves are identical over their whole range, not whether their AUCs differ.

rocCurve

Display ROC curve plot

aucTable

Display AUC summary table

cutoffTable

Display detailed cutoff analysis

optimalCutoffs

Display optimal cutoff summary

diagnosticMetrics

Display comprehensive diagnostic metrics

clinicalMetrics

Display clinical application metrics (PPV, NPV, LR+, LR-)

smoothMethod

Method for smoothing ROC curves

partialAuc

Calculate partial AUC for specific sensitivity/specificity ranges

partialAucType

Whether to calculate pAUC over a specificity or sensitivity range

partialAucFrom

Lower end of the partial AUC range, on the specificity or sensitivity scale chosen above, for example 0.8 for high specificity.

partialAucTo

Upper end of the partial AUC range; it must be greater than the lower end.

crocAnalysis

Calculate Concentrated ROC curves for early retrieval analysis

crocAlpha

Concentration parameter for CROC exponential magnifier function

convexHull

Calculate the ROC convex hull (operating points reachable by randomly mixing two cut-offs; in-sample, so optimistic)

detectImbalance

Automatically detect class imbalance and recommend PRC when appropriate

imbalanceThreshold

Ratio threshold for imbalance detection (e.g., 3.0 means 3:1 or 1:3 ratio)

showImbalanceWarning

Add the explanatory detail to the class-imbalance warning. The warning itself is always shown when imbalance is detected; this only controls how much it explains.

recommendPRC

Recommend adding the Precision-Recall curve alongside the ROC curve when imbalance is detected.

prevalence

Disease prevalence to assume when computing predictive values. Used only when "Use observed prevalence" is unticked - set it to the prevalence of the population the test will actually be used in, which for a screening setting is usually far lower than in a case-control sample.

useObservedPrevalence

Compute PPV, NPV and the clinical impact metrics at the prevalence observed in these data (the default). Untick it to assume a different prevalence instead - appropriate when the sample is enriched for cases and does not reflect the population the test will be used in. The prevalence actually used is printed in the results.

clinicalContext

Clinical application context for interpretation

clinicalPresets

Sets how the optimal cutoff is searched for: each preset turns Youden index optimization on and sets the minimums (Screening: sensitivity 0.90; Diagnostic validation: 0.80 and 0.80; Confirmatory: specificity 0.95; Research: keeps the minimums you enter, so it differs from Custom only by switching Youden optimization on). No other option changes. The controls a preset overrides are greyed while it is selected.

comprehensive_output

Include comprehensive statistical details

clinical_interpretation

Provide clinical context for ROC analysis results

showAnalysisSummary

A plain-language summary of the main results: the best AUC with its interval and the cutoff with its sensitivity and specificity. Internal validation results appear in the same panel whenever Internal validation is ticked.

showClinicalReport

Copy-ready Methods and Results sentences built from these results. Check them against the tables before pasting them into a report.

showTableNotes

Show explanatory notes and cell footnotes below the results tables, including methods, definitions and cautions for reading each table. The random seed of a resampled result is always shown.

plotTheme

Visual theme for the ROC plots. "jamovi (follow global)" draws them with the theme chosen in jamovi, like every other plot in the document. Classic, Modern and Clinical adjust the grid lines and border on top of it.

plotWidth

Width of ROC plots

plotHeight

Height of ROC plots

showCutoffPoints

Highlight optimal cutoff points on ROC curve

showConfidenceBands

Display confidence bands around ROC curve

showMetricsDiff

Display detailed differences between model metrics

statisticalComparison

Perform comprehensive statistical comparison between models

calibrationAnalysis

Assess calibration (agreement between observed and predicted probabilities)

calibrationPlot

Display the calibration plot: observed proportion against predicted probability in the Hosmer-Lemeshow risk groups, with an optional flexible spline curve (splineCalibration)

hosmerLemeshow

Perform Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test

hlGroups

Number of equal-sized risk groups used both for the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and for binning the calibration plot

brierScore

Calculate Brier score and scaled Brier score

calibrationMetrics

Calculate calibration slope, intercept, and calibration-in-the-large

splineCalibration

Fit a flexible calibration curve by logistic regression of the outcome on a natural cubic spline of the logit of the predicted probability, a variant of the flexible calibration curves of Austin & Steyerberg (2019), who used loess and restricted cubic splines on the probability scale. Adds the smooth curve to the calibration plot and the integrated calibration index (ICI, the mean absolute difference between the curve and the diagonal) with E50, E90 and Emax to the calibration summary. Requires calibrationAnalysis.

splineKnots

Knots of the spline calibration curve (3 to 7). The spline has knots - 1 degrees of freedom; more knots follow the data more closely but need more events per knot. Used only when splineCalibration is on.

eoRatio

Expected/Observed ratio for overall calibration. Reported only when the predictor is supplied as a probability in 0 to 1; when a logistic model has to be fitted here to get probabilities the ratio is 1 by construction and the cell is left blank.

calibrationDensity

Overlay the distribution of predicted probabilities along the bottom of the calibration plot, so a calibration point backed by two patients is not read like one backed by two hundred. Skipped when there are fewer than 10 usable probabilities to smooth.

multiClassROC

Enable multi-class ROC analysis for outcomes with >2 levels

multiClassStrategy

Strategy for multi-class ROC analysis

multiClassAveraging

Method for averaging AUC across classes. Both averages are reported side by side for the One-vs-Rest strategy: Macro weights every class equally, Weighted weights each class by how many cases it contains. The One-vs-One strategy reports only its own unweighted average over class pairs, which is what that statistic is defined as. Both averages are always shown, so this setting changes no displayed value; with One-vs-One, Weighted only raises a notice.

clinicalImpact

Calculate observed or projected workload at independently supplied score cutoffs

nntCalculation

Show inverse net benefit and inverse Youden index; neither is a count of tests or reviews

clinicalUtilityCurve

Display clinical utility curve showing test consequences

decisionImpactTable

Show decision impact at various thresholds

internalValidation

Perform internal validation using cross-validation or bootstrap

validationMethod

Bootstrap: Harrell's optimism-corrected AUC of a logistic model of the marker (resamples holding one outcome group are dropped and counted). Cross-validation: stratified 10-fold, or one fold per patient of the smaller outcome group when it has fewer than 10, reporting the mean fold AUC and the SD across folds, which is not a standard error.

decisionImpactCurves

Plot the clinical impact curve: how many of 1000 tested patients would be called high risk at each threshold probability, and how many of those actually have the event.

impactCutoffs

Fixed score cutoffs on the marker's own scale, comma separated. The default 0.5 is meant for predicted probabilities (Prediction scale = probability); for a raw marker enter cutoffs inside its observed range. A warning names any cutoff that classifies every analyzed patient the same way.

utilityThreshold

Threshold probability for net benefit: the risk at which a clinician is indifferent between acting and not acting, so its odds are the harm of a false positive relative to the benefit of a true positive (0.1 means one true positive is worth nine false positives). Used by the clinical impact and workload tables; it is not a score cutoff.

workloadPopulationSize

Size of the population the projected workload counts are scaled to. Used for every projected row: the main prevalence when Observed prevalence is unticked, and every additional target prevalence. Observed rows count the analyzed patients instead.

analysisUnit

What one row is (slide, core, patient...). Printed in the frozen-model report; every analyzed row weighs equally in its metrics.

prevalenceScenarios

Extra target-population prevalences, as proportions between 0 and 1 separated by commas (for example 0.05, 0.2). Each adds projected rows to the workload table at the same fixed cutoffs. Leave blank for none; an unreadable entry is ignored with a warning.

validationPanel

Evaluates an already-fitted model or score at prespecified fixed cutoffs, without refitting or choosing a cutoff from these data, and replaces every other output with the validation context, denominator ledger and frozen-model metrics. Needs a positive class, an explicit negative level, an explicit Direction and the fixed score cutoffs.

validationNegative

The outcome level that means the condition is absent. Required by the frozen-model report, which refuses any outcome level that is neither this nor the positive class instead of pooling it as negative.

referenceDescription

Free text describing the reference standard and whether its readers were blinded to the score (for example histology, blinded). Printed in the frozen-model validation context.

modelVersion

Identifier of the fitted model or score version being evaluated. Required when Cohort role is frozen, so the report names exactly which model the metrics belong to.

cohortRole

Declared by you and printed in the frozen-model report; the analysis does not check it. A value left at its default is printed as (default setting).

samplingDesign

Declared by you and printed in the frozen-model report; the analysis does not check it. A value left at its default is printed as (default setting). The default is Other / unknown so that an untouched report does not assert a sampling design; how PPV and NPV should be read depends on it.

thresholdSource

Declared by you and printed in the frozen-model report; the analysis does not check it. A value left at its default is printed as (default setting).

predictionScale

What the predictor values are. Score (default) is any marker or model score: the calibration summary and plot, Brier score, E/O ratio, Hosmer-Lemeshow test and the decision and clinical impact curves then use risks from a logistic model of the score fitted to these data (in-sample). Probability means the values are predicted probabilities of the selected positive class, assessed as supplied; a predictor with a value outside 0 to 1 gets none of those outputs, and a probability is never reversed. Values between 0 and 1 are not taken as probabilities unless this says so. Frozen-model validation uses the same setting.

patientID

Patient identifier. On the main analysis it is used only to warn when a patient has several rows: every panel except the Frozen-model validation report treats each row as an independent patient, so their intervals and tests are too narrow then. Only the Frozen-model validation report resamples whole patients.

siteID

Optional site or center of each row. The frozen-model report then adds one set of metrics per site, conditional on the observed sites, and resamples within sites. Every row needs a site, and a patient may not appear at two sites.

partitionID

Optional development or validation label of each row, used by the frozen-model report to check that no patient appears in more than one partition (leakage). Requires a patient identifier.

validationBootstrap

Adds percentile confidence intervals to the frozen-model metrics, resampling whole patients when a patient identifier is given (jointly across models, within sites). Without it the report shows point estimates only.

validationDraws

Number of patient-level bootstrap replicates for the frozen-model intervals. Separate from Bootstrap samples, which serves the other panels.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# pROC::aSAH ships with pROC, an Import, so the example runs in every module that
# carries this analysis. positiveClass and validationNegative are Level options: always
# required arguments (validationNegative = NULL unless the frozen-model report is used).
enhancedROC(
    data = pROC::aSAH,
    outcome = "outcome",
    positiveClass = "Poor",
    validationNegative = NULL,
    predictors = c("s100b", "ndka"))
} # }
